name: Anal Fistula

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Anal Fistula

criteria.description: Presence of an external perianal skin opening with intermittent discharge
Identification of an internal anal canal opening on examination or imaging
Demonstration of a fistulous tract by MRI, endoanal ultrasound, or fistulography
Signs of perianal inflammation such as erythema or induration

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of an external opening with discharge plus identification of an internal opening or fistula tract on imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: MRI is considered the gold standard imaging modality for fistula tract delineation.

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers (e.g., ESR, CRP) in active infection
imaging: MRI pelvis showing fistulous tract and internal opening
other: Clinical examination revealing external opening and induration
Anoscopy or proctoscopy to identify internal opening

distinguishingFeatures: Abscess presents as a painful, fluctuant swelling without a chronic fistulous tract
Usually acute onset with systemic signs of infection
Presence of other gastrointestinal symptoms such as diarrhea and abdominal pain
Histologic and endoscopic evidence of transmural inflammation
Multiple complex fistulas and associated perianal skin tags

redFlags: Rapidly worsening perianal pain with systemic signs of infection
Signs suggestive of malignancy within fistula tract (e.g., bleeding, mass)
references: Parks AG, et al. 'A classification of fistula-in-ano.' Br J Surg. 1976.
American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons Clinical Practice Guidelines for Anal Fistula.
Mahadevan U, et al. 'Management of perianal fistulizing Crohn’s disease.' Gastroenterology. 2020.
